question: What the green pointer beside a moving unit's counter is, where it is drawn and which way it points.

addresses.name: CUnit::FaceNextProvince
addresses.comment: **Turns a moving unit towards the next province of its path.** Takes the unit point of the province it is in and of the path's first province (slot 30), asks 0xC0BDBA for the angle between them with the map's width, takes pi/2 off, stores the result at +0x104 and +0x108 and hands it to the avatar's slot 37, CHoiAvatar::SetRotation - which turns the figure and the `counter_arrow` pointer of both counters. Does nothing for a unit with no province or no path. Called by CUnit::ShowMoving and by CUnit::AdvanceMovement after an arrival that leaves a path. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end: the two slot 30 calls (+0x78) on [esi+0x130] and on `map->provinces[*[esi+0x138]]`, the call of 0xC0BDBA with `map->+0x2A74`, the subtraction of the double at 0x160A2A0 (pi/2), the two stores and the indirect call through [[esi+0x164]+0x94]. Bare `ret`, the unit in ESI.

addresses.name: CUnit::SetHeading
addresses.no_signature: the unit in EAX and the angle in XMM0
addresses.comment: Stores an angle at CUnit +0x108 and +0x104 and hands it to the avatar's slot 37, CHoiAvatar::SetRotation, where the unit has an avatar. CUnit::AdvanceMovement and CUnit::CancelMovement call it when a unit comes to a stop. The name is ours. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end, six instructions: the two `movss` stores of xmm0, the test of [eax+0x164] and the call through its +0x94.

addresses.name: CHoiAvatar::SetRotation
addresses.comment: **CHoiAvatar slot 37.** Gives the angle to the `counter_arrow` billboard of the far counter (`[+0x13C]->+0x1B4`) and of the near one (`[+0x140]->+0x1B4`), each through its own slot 37, CBillboardObject::SetRotation, and then to the figure (+0x124) - less `[+0x14C]` times a constant where the byte +0x151 is set. So a moving unit's pointer and its figure are turned together. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: Read end to end: the three indirect calls through +0x94, on `[[ecx+0x13c]+0x1b4]`, `[[ecx+0x140]+0x1b4]` and `[ecx+0x124]`, and the `cmp byte ptr [ecx+0x151],0` before the last. `ret 4`. vtable.py puts 0x84AC70 at slot 37 of CHoiAvatar.

addresses.name: CBillboardObject::Draw
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CBillboardObject::Draw(CBillboardObject* this@ESI, void* graphics@stack:4, void* device@stack:8, float* matrix@stack:12, float time@stack:16)
addresses.comment: Draws one billboard: for a type of more than two frames it steps the frame it shows by the clock, and then calls the type's slot 31, CBillboardType::DrawQuad, with the frame (+0x150), the rotation (+0xB24) and the scale. A two-frame type such as `counter_arrow` keeps the frame it was given. The name is ours; likely, read in the decompiled C. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: The decompiled C: `type->slot34() > 2` guarding the frame arithmetic on +0x150 and +0x154, and the call through [type+0x7c] with `[esi+0xb24]`. `ret 0x10`, the object in ESI.

addresses.name: CBillboardType::DrawQuad
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CBillboardType::DrawQuad(CBillboardType* this, int animationFrame, void* graphics, void* device, float* matrix, float time, short mode, int a, int column, bool flip, float rotation, int b, float scale)
addresses.comment: **Slot 31 of the billboard type: where a billboard goes and how it is turned.** Builds `T * R * inverse(view rotation)` and places it at the object's position, T a translation of [this+0xF8] along x - the declaration's `offset`, inferred - and R `D3DXMatrixRotationZ(rotation)`. Translation first, rotation second: the picture stands `offset` from the object **in the direction it is turned to**. Sets the shader's `vMultiplier`, `WorldMatrix`, `vXOffset` (the frame's column), `vScale` and `vFlip`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: `movss xmm2,[esi+0xf8]` stored at the matrix's m41; `D3DXMatrixRotationZ` at 0xB0781A; `D3DXMatrixMultiply(&R, &T, &R)` at 0xB078B5 by the order of its three pushes; `D3DXMatrixInverse` of the view; the literals 'WorldMatrix', 'vXOffset', 'vScale', 'vFlip', 'vMultiplier'. `ret 0x30`. And a screenshot of the running game: the pointer lies on the line it points along, to the degree.

addresses.name: CBillboardType::LoadKey
addresses.signature: void __thiscall CBillboardType::LoadKey(CBillboardType* this, CParseContext* parse, SaveToken key)
addresses.comment: **Slot 4 of the table at VA 0x1605258: the keys of a `billboardType`.** `noOfFrames` to +0xF0, `font` to +0x114, `textureFile` to +0x9C, `effect` to +0xB8, `effectFile` to +0xD4, `font_size` to +0x104 through `sscanf`; `scale`, `offset` and `offset2` go to two list readers (0xA7B640, 0xA7B070) whose destinations the decompilation loses. Anything else goes to the base class's loader. The record had this slot as read by nobody. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
addresses.evidence: The switch on the token: 0x1B, 0x1D, 0x24, 0x58, 0x59, 0x5C, 0x161, 0x17F and 0x182, which saveTokens.json names noOfFrames, font, textureFile, effect, effectFile, scale, offset, offset2 and font_size. `ret 8`.

struct_fields.name: heading
struct_fields.comment: Which way the unit faces: the angle from its province's unit point to the next province's, less pi/2, as CUnit::FaceNextProvince works it out. Its avatar's figure and the pointer beside its counter are turned by it. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
struct_fields.evidence: The store at +0x104 in 0x5CB520 and 0x5CB4F0; FINDINGS-gui.md already has CCombat::UpdateCombatStatusWindow reading `units[0]->+0x104 + pi/2`.

struct_fields.name: heading_copy
struct_fields.comment: Written with the same angle as `heading` (+0x104) by both of its writers, one instruction apart. What reads this one apart from that was not looked for. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.

struct_fields.name: arrows_shown
struct_fields.comment: Set to 1 by CUnit::ShowMoving when it sets `shows_arrow` on both of the avatar's counters, so that it is done once. What clears it was not read. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-counters.md, section 9.
struct_fields.evidence: `cmp byte ptr [eax+0x150],1` then the two stores of 1 at `[[eax+0x13c]+0x1b8]` and `[[eax+0x140]+0x1b8]` and at +0x150 itself, at the end of 0x5C9E10.

slots_noted: CBillboardType has no RTTI entry; its slots 4 and 31 are given in the comments
